contradictions.detail: The original description stated a dual-range transfer case. A commenter showed the car lacks the low-range control and BaT updated the listing, so the corrected listing now describes a single-speed unit.

The October 2025 invoice ties the right-front footwell water to clearing the sunroof drains. The seller's comment attributes it to the plastic cowl piece at the base of the windshield letting water into the climate intake. The two explanations differ; the invoices should show which repair was actually done.

documentation.rationale: Identity is solid: the VIN is listed and decodes cleanly, and the Carfax snapshot shows 24 service entries. Several October 2025 invoices are cited by date. However, the key cooling work is relayed as dealer statement, and nothing on the chain, EAS, ZF fluid, scan or bumper repaint is documented.

condition.rationale: Photos show a tidy exterior, clean interior and clean engine bay, with fresh front brakes and tires claimed. Against that: a documented water-intrusion episode in the right-front footwell, a repainted rear bumper of unknown cause, and visible underside surface rust. Expensive systems remain unproven either way.

price_value.rationale: The likely hammer sits around or below the $13,222 fair-value midpoint. That is offset by six owners including fleet use, base trim without the HD/low-range pack, and the water-intrusion history, all of which lower risk-adjusted value.

mission_fit.rationale: Jason needs a fun manual daily driver. This is an automatic SUV in a branch the current state lists as deprioritized, his mechanic will not work on Land Rovers, and the RX already covers utility. Without low range, even the capability case is weaker.

logistics.rationale: San Rafael is a short drive from Pacific Grove. It is a dealer seller on a CA title with no extra dealer fees, so a mobile or local PPI is plausible, though access before the close is not confirmed.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Aintree Green over Almond with Walnut is an attractive combination. That is offset by base trim, no HD package or low range, and refinished black wheels; overall a typical example.

ppi_focus: Overnight-cold start with audio: listen for 1-3 seconds of chain rattle, and read cam/crank correlation values and P0016-P0018 history.
Inspect the coolant crossover pipes under the supercharger and the thermostat/water pump area for staining or original plastic.
Lift the right-front carpet: check padding moisture, connector corrosion and the cowl/plenum seal, and water-test the sunroof drains.
Cycle the EAS through all heights; time compressor run, check for faults, and leak-down overnight.
Take paint-meter readings on the rear bumper and all panels; look for impact evidence behind the rear bumper.
Check underside corrosion at the rear crossmember, hitch, sills and brake lines on this Florida/Texas car.
Check ZF 8HP fluid condition and lock-up shudder at 1,200-1,600 rpm.
Check rear diff whine, driveshaft center bearing and front lower arm bushings.
Check the fuel tank flange for seepage and confirm recall completion.
Run a full module scan including SRS, parking brake and HVAC actuators, cold and hot.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: invoices confirming crossover pipe and cooling work plus a dry, corrosion-free footwell after a water test.
Up: a clean all-module scan and PPI with healthy EAS and no chain codes.
Down: moisture or connector corrosion in the right-front footwell, or SRS/BCM faults.
Down: the rear bumper repaint tied to an impact with hidden damage, or chain-correlation codes or EAS faults found at inspection.
Independently of condition: an automatic, deprioritized LR4 does not address the current manual-sports-car search.
evidence.mission_note: This is an automatic utility SUV in a deprioritized branch, and Jason's mechanic will not service Land Rovers. It does not solve the need for a fun manual daily, and the RX already supplies family utility. Lacking low range, it adds little capability the RX lacks beyond seven seats and a roof rack.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN decodes as a 2016 LR4 3.0 supercharged V6, the odometer agrees with the Carfax snapshot at 74,965, and a CA title and 24 Carfax service entries are cited. Observed issues are a six-owner history including fleet use, a repainted rear bumper of undisclosed cause, surface rust under the rear, and an Oct 2025 invoice documenting water under the right-front footwell, with two differing explanations from the invoice and the seller. October 2025 brake and headlight work is dated; the thermostat, water pump and hose work is relayed as dealer statement without the crossover pipes named. Timing chain condition, EAS health, transmission fluid history and an all-module scan remain undocumented, and the posted cold-start video was not examined here. Photos show a clean engine bay and interior and attractive Aintree Green over Almond, but the car is base trim without low range. Two attached images depict unrelated vehicles and were disregarded.
evidence.next_action: Request the October 2025 invoices (cooling work and footwell repair), a printed all-module scan, and confirmation that a mobile PPI in San Rafael can be completed before the Monday 2026-11-09 close.

recalls.summary: Jaguar Land Rover North America, LLC (Land Rover) is recalling certain 2010-2013 Range Rover Sport and 2010-2016 LR4 vehicles equipped with 3.0L V6 or 5.0L V8 engines.  The fuel outlet flange mounted on the fuel tank may crack, possibly resulting in a fuel leak.

Jaguar Land Rover North America, LLC (Land Rover) is recalling certain model year 2016 Land Rover LR4 vehicles manufactured May 3, 2016 through May 10, 2016.  The affected vehicles have driver side frontal air bags that may not inflate properly.
